analysis.title: Paul Donovan's daily audio: Inflation fantasies
key_insights: US October CPI is due. The element of guesswork in calculating inflation has risen recently, and the absence of October 2025 data (a legacy of the 2025 government shutdown) removes the comparison base.
Consumers are likely to perceive inflation as higher than reported, given the importance placed on high-frequency purchases.

Inflation from the Gulf war has appeared just as inflation from tariffs was falling out of the consumer price calculations. Since the pandemic there have been four temporary inflation shocks in quick succession.
No second-round inflation effects (in particular no wage-price spiral) have appeared despite the look of continuous inflation, which argues against a structural inflation bias.
Trump's reiteration of a very low chance of strikes against Iran has helped keep oil prices low.
The prospect of Defense Secretary Hegseth facing impeachment may encourage investor speculation. If Hegseth were a scapegoat for the war, a diplomatic solution might be easier.
Central bank speakers on the agenda include Waller (US) and Lane (Europe).
